alternatingChange.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The dense upper-left cluster at 2500 breaks into separated small fragments by 3000, while band1 gains a tall upper-middle branching arrangement and more lower-edge occupied structure. The intervening gaps and occupied tiles visibly change, not just colors or food shading.

seasonalChanges.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. In majority-fed band1, small lower clusters expand into a broad dense middle-lower branching mass, and an upper ladder-like cluster grows. In minority-fed band0, the large lower-left lattice and much of the upper-left branching mass clear into widely separated fragments. This matches the qualifying band1 growth and band0 retreat.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Majority-fed band0 grows a dense upper-left branching cluster from a small upper fragment. Minority-fed band1 loses most of its central-lower dense mass, leaving large clear gaps and smaller upper and bottom clusters. This matches the qualifying band0 growth and band1 retreat.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. Majority-fed band1 develops a taller upper-middle branching arrangement and expanded lower-edge structure. Minority-fed band0 loses most of its dense upper-left cluster, leaving sparse disconnected groups of separate organisms. This matches qualifying band1 growth and band0 retreat.

sameAgeComparisons.observation: Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The historical world has a dense vertical belt near the left edge and no band1 bodies. The foothold world has distinct upper and lower groups in both bands, including a lower-left lattice and lower band1 branching cluster.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The historical world has only small upper-left and lower-left fragments and no band1 bodies. The foothold world retains left-side fragments and has substantial upper and middle-lower clusters in band1.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The historical world regrows upper-left branching bodies and a lower-left lattice but still has no band1 bodies. The foothold world has a dense upper-left cluster plus smaller upper and bottom groups in band1.

Not blind: the historical reference and numerical outcome are known. The historical world is sparse and band1 remains empty. The foothold world has sparse band0 groups and broad upper-middle and lower branching structures in band1. This is a one-seed descriptive difference, not general superiority.
